description: owine/* baseline — supply-chain hardened defaults. Pin everything, soak releases, escalate CVEs.

schedule: on monday, wednesday, friday and sunday

packageRules.description: Reclaim `deps:` as the baseline commit type. The top-level `semanticCommitType: deps` above is INERT on its own: Renovate ships two built-in default packageRules — `{matchPackageNames:['*'] => chore}` and `{matchDepTypes:['dependencies','require'] => fix}` — and packageRules ALWAYS beat top-level config, so without this override every bump commits as `chore:` (npm prod deps as `fix:`). That matters because release-please treats `chore:` as a HIDDEN, non-releasing type: Dockerfile/Actions/apk repos would cut zero releases and add nothing to the changelog. This catch-all re-forces `deps:` for every package (release-please recognizes `deps` as a releasable unit => patch, in a dedicated Dependencies changelog section). Ordered FIRST so the more specific rules below/after still win where they match: lock file maintenance => chore, CI/Actions => ci, security => fix (vulnerabilityAlerts, force). Nothing in this fleet types a dependency update `feat:` — majors included; see the major rule below.

Lock file maintenance commits as `chore:` — the ONE update type that must NOT cut a release. It refreshes transitive/nested deps within existing manifest ranges (no direct-dependency change consumers can see) and runs 4x/week (mon/wed/fri/sun, see the lockFileMaintenance block). Under the `deps:` baseline above it is a release-please releasable unit => a patch release every refresh = pure changelog/version spam. `chore:` is release-please's HIDDEN, non-releasing type, so refreshes stay silent. Uses matchUpdateTypes:['lockFileMaintenance'] (not matchPackageNames) because the maintenance branch has no depName; ordered AFTER the catch-all so it wins over `* => deps`.

Major bumps — separate PR per package, 7-day soak, manual review required. Deliberately sets NO semanticCommitType: it falls through to the `* => deps` catch-all above and cuts a PATCH release, in the changelog's Dependencies section alongside routine churn. This rule used to type majors `feat:` (minor release, Features section); that is gone, because `feat:` should mean a feature someone here wrote, not an upstream version number crossing a line — inflating consumers' minor versions on dependency churn made the minor digit meaningless. Nothing Renovate generates is `feat:` any more. What still marks a major as special is the review surface, not the commit type: its own branch (separateMajorMinor/separateMultipleMajor), a 7-day soak, automerge off, and the `major-update`/`needs-review` labels. Also still not `feat!:`/breaking: an upstream major is not automatically the consumer's breaking change.

CI plumbing commits as `ci:` — release-please's HIDDEN, non-releasing type. Actions, reusable workflows and composite `action.yml` files are build-time infrastructure: nothing a consumer of the published image/package/server can observe, so bumping actions/checkout should neither cut a patch release nor add a changelog line. Ordered AFTER the `* => deps` catch-all and the major rule so it wins for every update type, major included — a GHA major still gets that rule's 7-day soak, `automerge: false` and `major-update`/`needs-review` labels, it just doesn't release. Security is exempt automatically: `vulnerabilityAlerts.semanticCommitType: fix` is applied at force level and beats every packageRule, so a CVE in an action still lands in Bug Fixes and cuts a release. Covers `.github/workflows`, `.github/actions`, `workflow-templates/` and any `action.yml` — the github-actions manager's own file patterns.

Same `ci:` treatment for the workflow version literals the customManagers block below extracts — tool versions in matrix arrays, run-step args and env defaults inside `.github/workflows/*.yml`. Those deps belong to the custom regex manager, not `github-actions`, so the matchManagers rule above can't reach them; they are matched by path instead. Deliberately NOT `matchManagers: ['custom.regex']`, which would also silence any unrelated custom manager a consumer repo defines.
Pin Docker image and GitHub Action digests so a re-tagged image/action can't slip in
docker-compose: bump tags but never pin digests — keeps compose files readable for humans editing them by hand

Node version pins use LTS-aware versioning — Renovate's 'node' versioning scheme tracks LTS lines (22, 24, 26, ...) and skips Current/odd-numbered releases (23, 25, 27, ...). LTS-to-LTS major bumps still come as separate manual-review PRs via the major-bump rule above.

customManagers.description: Bump version literals in GitHub Actions workflows annotated with `# renovate: datasource=X depName=Y`. Supports trailing-comment (hint after value) and leading-comment (hint on line above value) styles. INVARIANT: inter-field separators must use `[ \t]`, never `\s` — `\s` matches `\n` and causes cross-block attribution (see PR #4). The two patterns share textually identical metadata-tail and value subpatterns; JSON has no interpolation and RE2 has no subpattern references, so edits must apply character-for-character to both. Reaches places the github-actions manager can't natively (matrix arrays, run-step args, env defaults).
